verdict_reason: Both estimands are implemented exactly and both are emitted. The manuscript's pooled Spearman (sections/metrics_geometry.tex:246-251, one rho_S over every causal {i,j} pair per head, mean over heads) is computed at positional_decay.py:192-237 and matches an independent rank-then-Pearson reference over 50 randomised causal heads at a maximum absolute difference of 0.000000000000e+00; the rowwise kernel matches an independent tie-averaged reference over 300 rows (ties injected in 1/3 of them) at 1.11e-16. The headline `mean_positional_decay_correlation` is deliberately the ROWWISE mean, and the measurement settles that this is right and the PAPER should change: on an exactly uniform causal attention pattern -- no positional preference by construction -- the manuscript's pooled statistic reads -0.4344766895 (L=8), -0.4571393525 (16), -0.4659740104 (64), -0.4664886660 (128), -0.4666215371 (256) where the correct answer is 0, while the rowwise reads EXACTLY 0.0 at every length. On real gpt2 (eager, fp32, the shipped 5 WikiText passages of 157/154/83/71/62 tokens) the pooled value is -0.5074500340 and the uniform null at those same five lengths is -0.4662742429, so 91.9% of the manuscript's statistic is causal-mask geometry and only -0.0412 is attributable to the model. The rowwise is not merely insensitive: on an exp(-0.3 d) decaying head it reads -1.0000000000 against the pooled -0.9997312664, so it detects real decay at full strength. Both quantities are emitted under distinct names, so nothing silently stands in for the other.
comparable_reason: Every key in this family is diluted by depth. Inserting function-preserving IDENTITY attention layers alongside one genuinely decaying head moves the headline -1.0 -> -0.5 -> -0.25 -> -0.125 -> -0.0625 -> -0.03125 for L = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 -- exactly -1/L, since the mean is taken over layers -- with Spearman(depth) = +1.000 for the rowwise, the pooled AND the demoted nosink twin. The pooled key is worse still: its value is dominated by a model-independent offset that depends only on the sequence-length distribution (-0.4345 at L=8 rising to -0.4666 at L=256), so a corpus change moves it as much as a model change. The raw rowwise value also mixes decay with attention-sink strength, which is model-specific: I measure `_meta_attention_sink_mass` = 0.4691734215 on gpt2, i.e. 46.9% of every causal row's mass sits at position 0, which is simultaneously the maximum-distance key. The task states this itself and emits the sink-excluded control, but that control fails the same depth test.
github_reason: No code was ever released for this quantity. `task_metadata.py` cites RoFormer (Su et al. 2021) for the decay premise and ALiBi (Press et al. 2021) for context; neither paper releases a distance-vs-attention Spearman implementation, and the statistic is BLME's own construction. In place of a released reference I built two independent implementations from the definition -- a rank-then-Pearson pooled reference over every causal {i,j} pair, and a tie-averaged per-row reference -- and the shipped branches agree with them at 0.00e+00 and 1.11e-16 respectively.
paper_reason: There is no published scalar for this quantity anywhere in the chain. The BLME manuscript's positional-decay subsection contains one defining equation and zero result values; RoFormer plots a long-term-decay curve of an upper bound on the inner product, not a rank correlation on trained attention; ALiBi plots perplexity against extrapolation length. What IS reproducible is the analytic null, and it is reproduced exactly: a uniform causal pattern must give 0, and the shipped headline gives 0.0 exactly at L = 8, 16, 64, 128 and 256, while the manuscript's own estimand gives -0.4345 to -0.4666.
confounds_reason: Depth, sequence length and the attention sink, in that order; width is not a term (a Spearman over attention probabilities has no d_model in it). The identity-block intervention above is a mechanical proof of the depth term: the value is exactly -1/L for a fixed set of informative heads, rho(depth) = +1.000 for all three emitted variants. The length term is mechanical too and applies only to the pooled key: the uniform null moves -0.4344766895 -> -0.4666215371 as L goes 8 -> 256. On gpt2 the sink carries 46.9% of causal-row mass at the maximum-distance position, and the raw-minus-nosink gap is -0.3033978474 vs -0.4245932049, i.e. 0.1212 of the reported number is sink strength rather than decay.
defects: PAPER (not code): sections/metrics_geometry.tex:246-251 defines rho_pos as one pooled Spearman per head. That estimand is NOT null-calibrated -- it reads -0.4666215371 on an exactly uniform causal pattern at L=256 and accounts for 91.9% of the gpt2 value -- because pooling triangular causal entries confounds distance with row normalisation: a uniform row's entries shrink as the context grows, so long distances (which occur only in deep rows) are systematically paired with small values. The code is right; the manuscript must be reconciled to the rowwise definition (already tracked in RERUN_LEDGER.md).

DOMAIN, positional_decay.py:193-208: the pooled branch runs q >= 1 WITH the diagonal, the rowwise branch q >= 3 WITHOUT it (`range(2, seq_len)` plus a `_row.size <= 2` skip). Part of the 0.204 gap between the two gpt2 values (-0.3033978474 vs -0.5074500340) is therefore a domain difference rather than purely an estimand difference. Emitting a rowwise-domain pooled twin would separate the two effects; `layer_positional_decay` also has no per-layer pooled counterpart.

CONFIG/SCOPE, defaults.yaml (num_samples: 5) and positional_decay.py:119 (max_length=256): the manuscript scopes this metric to a 'long-context regime' and says short sequences are dominated by sampling noise and causal-mask geometry. The five scored WikiText passages are 157/154/83/71/62 tokens -- none reaches the 256 cap, and the mean is 105.4. The shipped protocol does not meet the manuscript's own applicability condition.

CODE/GUARD, positional_decay.py:107: the fp32 promotion is skipped above 2,000,000,000 parameters, so the metric is discontinuous in parameter count. The code's own comment records that in bf16 20.88% of pythia-70m rows come out exactly flat and the headline moves -10.89%; a >2B bf16 checkpoint is measured in that regime while a 1.9B one is not. `_meta_promoted_to_fp32` records which side of the line a run fell on, which is the right diagnostic, but the discontinuity remains.

CODE/POLICY, positional_decay.py:50-51: an exactly flat row returns the null 0.0 rather than None, i.e. an undefined Spearman is mapped to a legal correlation value. This is what makes the uniform null read exactly 0.0 and is the right convention for THIS estimand, but it is inert at the shipped protocol (`_meta_n_flat_attn_rows` = 0 on gpt2 in fp32) and would silently attenuate the mean in a low-precision run. The count is emitted, which is the necessary safeguard.

CODE/DIAGNOSTIC, positional_decay.py:167-168: `_n_nonfinite_attn_rows` scans every row of the square matrix, including the masked future cells that are never scored, and no scored-row denominator is emitted alongside it.
COMPARABILITY (not a fidelity defect): all three emitted variants are exactly -1/L under identity-block insertion, so none is usable as a cross-depth feature without an explicit depth control.
